title: Swedish butterfly counts in 2010-2025 had the British cool-range sign for previous-summer warmth in all main models, but year-permutation tests did not confirm a site or species-niche effect
abstract: Question: two campaign publications found that a warm previous summer raised next-year UK butterfly counts more at the cool side of ranges, but disagreed whether a species-niche effect (sci:e56749e3) or plain site climate (sci:c636c268) causes it. Does the pattern repeat in an independent network, and which mechanism does it follow? Data: Swedish Butterfly Monitoring Scheme (SeBMS v1.13, CC0), 57 taxa, 408 sites, 62,919 site-year indices in 2010-2024 from a flight-curve method; E-OBS v32.0e summer temperature; CLIMBER European niches. Method: plan written before the fits. M1 (replication): taxon x site and taxon x year fixed effects, previous-summer anomaly x position. M2 (new between-species design): taxon x site and site x year fixed effects, so only taxa at the same site and year are compared; the earlier site x year test kept taxon x year effects, which remove most of a species-niche effect when the anomaly is national. Two-way clustered intervals, 999 year-relabel and taxon-relabel permutations. Result: all seven main interactions had the British sign. M1 with the European niche position (TNPgdd) gave -17.9 (95% interval -33.2 to -2.7; Britain -13.9), year-relabel p = 0.093. Site climate gave -4.1 (-7.7 to -0.6; Britain -4.85), p = 0.153. M2 gave -11.9 (-23.9 to +0.1), year-relabel p = 0.132, taxon-relabel p = 0.029; with annual-temperature positions -11.6 (-20.8 to -2.5), p = 0.099 and 0.005. Under the plan rules no hypothesis passed: replication and site climate were 'same sign, not clear', and the species-niche test was not supported. Estimates were stable to survey-weather adjustment, recorder effects and one-year jackknife, but near zero in 2010-2017. The M1 niche term had a negative placebo (-11.9); the M2 placebo was +0.4. Limitations: only 15 summers with mostly national anomalies; sparse visits; mostly southern and point sites; correlational design; no trait controls.

Dashed: British values. 95% two-way clustered intervals.
Year-relabel and taxon-relabel permutation nulls (999) with the observed estimates. No year-relabel p was below 0.05; the M2 taxon-relabel p was 0.029.
